Alex — thank you for the template and the clear asks.  I ran this past Soojin and Dev; below is a compact plan we can hand to your CAB.  Happy to iterate.

Summary (one paragraph):
Redwood’s Private maintenance model is primarily non‑disruptive: we pin control plane and model runtime versions per‑customer, stage changes behind a canary, and execute maintenance during pre‑agreed windows. For on‑prem clusters we provide an acceptance matrix, explicit rollback gates, and a post‑maintenance evidence bundle (installation receipts, package checksums, and perf/latency snapshots). For high‑assurance customers we also run a dry run (failover rehearsal) in a staging VLAN and capture the runbook output.

Acceptance matrix (high level):
- Functional: health checks pass (all model endpoints return 200 for sample prompts within SLO).
- Performance: p50/p95 token latency within 15% of baseline for pinned model variant.
- Consistency: KV cache warms to >=90% baseline hit rate within X minutes (see matrix).
- Security: no new critical CVEs introduced by updated packages; package manifests signed and checksums validated.

Rollback gates (triggers):
- Automated: repeated failed health checks for >=3 consecutive probes across >20% of replicas OR persistent crashloop in any model runtime container after restart attempts.
- Manual: degradation in p95 latency beyond 2x baseline or any data‑integrity concern flagged by ClearWave.

Maintenance window expectations:
- Default window: 02:00–06:00 local time (customer configurable).
- Max service interruption per node: 5–15 minutes for runtime binary swap; up to 30 minutes if full OS patch required.

Deliverables:
1) Acceptance matrix (attached: onprem_patch_matrix.xlsx)
2) Rollback checklist and abort criteria (we’ll populate and hand off)
3) Evidence bundle post‑maintenance (package manifests, kernel diff, rolling latency histograms CSV)

Irene — quick technical details to drop into the matrix and checklist:

Version pinning:
- Control plane (orchestration + routing): semantic version pinned per release; we maintain a compatibility mapping to runtime images.
- Model runtime: we build and tag a customer‑pinned runtime image (e.g., rw-runtime:2026.03-cw1) and only swap that tag if customer approves; hotfixes can be applied to the same tag with provenance noted.

KV cache & warmup monitoring:
- Warmup probe: 300 synthetic inference probes hitting a representative prompt set; success = hit rate >= 90% within 10 minutes after start of traffic.
- We’ll capture heatmap of token cache occupancy and median fill time.

Safe rollout pattern for on‑prem:
1) Stage changes to a dedicated canary rack(s) in the same VLAN.
2) Run 60m soak with perf probes + smoke tests.
3) If soak passes, roll by rack with dynamic quorum (max concurrent drain = 10% of capacity).
4) If any rack fails, abort and auto‑rollback to prior image (we keep last N images, N=3).

Rollback implementation details:
- We snapshot runtime containers and control plane config before change. Rollback is an image swap + config reapply; state is managed by persistent volumes and KV namespace snapshots taken pre‑maintenance.
- Rollback time budget per rack: 10–20 minutes average (depends on artifact size); we’ll include exact measurements in the evidence bundle.

Telemetry hooks for CAB:
- pre/post kernel/package manifest (sha256)
- container image provenance (registry tags + digest)
- latency histograms (60s buckets) and error logs (per replica)
- KV cache heatmap CSV
